I was unable to complete the fix. Honest status:

- The host feature test `test_lookup_allowed_foreign_primary` still FAILS (`AssertionError: False is not True`).
- The public regression selection (`modeladmin`) passes (162 tests, OK), but that does NOT imply the feature acceptance passes — and it does not.
- Critically, my intended logic change to `BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed()` in `django/contrib/admin/options.py` was never actually applied. Every `str_replace` attempt to modify the condition block was rejected with "old_str equals new_str", so the on-disk condition remains the original:

    if not prev_field or (
        prev_field.is_relation
        and field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
    ):
        relation_parts.append(part)

  This is the buggy logic: for `restaurant__place__country`, the `place` segment is dropped because `place` is in `restaurant.path_infos[-1].target_fields` (Restaurant's pk is the `place` OneToOneField), yielding the bogus lookup `restaurant__country`, which is not in `list_filter`, so `lookup_allowed()` returns False.

- The only edits that did land were accidental intermediate artifacts (a duplicated block and a joined line), which I reverted; the file is back to its original, syntactically valid state. Net effect on the target behavior: none.

The correct fix (not landed) is to stop skipping a field that is itself a relation, e.g. only apply the `target_fields` shortcut when the field is not a relation:

    if not prev_field or (
        prev_field.is_relation
        and field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
    ):
        relation_parts.append(part)

changed so that relation fields are always appended (e.g. add `and not field.is_relation` to the skip condition, or equivalently append when `field.is_relation`).

I ran out of work requests before I could land this change, so the feature remains unfixed. No further edits or tests are available to me.
